description.narrative:
OBJECTIVES: With the broader goal of preparing Ukraine for eventual post-war elections and EU integration, CEPPS proposes the PACE program with the following two objectives:
OBJECTIVE 1: Political parties begin to rebuild responsiveness and capacity ahead of potential elections.
Intermediate Result (IR) 1.1: Emerging and existing political parties and movement-based parties develop party platforms rooted in research and analysis and responsive to citizen interests in Ukraines wartime and post-war contexts
IR 1.2: Emerging and existing political parties and movements improve their institutional capacities to participate in elections and drive Ukraines ambitious recovery and democratic reform agenda
OBJECTIVE 2: Ukraines election administration gains skills, tools, knowledge, and resources to combat malign information influence and to effectively communicate with Ukrainian voters and electoral stakeholders ahead of post-war elections.
IR 2.1: Ukraines CEC advances a modern, strategic approach to communication and voter education with an eye to increased transparency, integrity, accessibility, and public engagement in elections

Projektet ”Pluralistic and Credible Elections in Ukraine” (PACE) syftar till att stärka grunden för framtida fria och rättvisa val i Ukraina genom att utveckla politiska partier, valadministrationens kapacitet, undersöka medborgarnas attityder och prioriteringar, samt bidra till inkluderande demokratiska processer. Insatsen sker under ett pågående krig, där institutioner är belastade, säkerhetsläget skiftar och demokratin är begränsad på grund av undantagstillstånd.

The project “Pluralistic and Credible Elections in Ukraine” (PACE) aims to strengthen the foundation for future free and fair elections in Ukraine by developing political parties, enhancing the capacity of the election administration, examining citizens’ attitudes and priorities, and contributing to inclusive democratic processes. The initiative is being carried out during an ongoing war, where institutions are under strain, security conditions fluctuate, and democracy is limited due to the state of emergency.
